outro.title: Move it with the arrow keys

lines.intro: In this lesson, you'll make your first shape appear: a teal circle, right in the middle of the game screen.
lines.tour: The lesson starts with two blocks: {start}when the game starts, and {sprite}define sprite player.
lines.looks: A sprite needs a look. Open the {click}Looks category.
lines.drag-look: Drag {grab}look like a circle into define sprite player. {snap}It snaps into place.
lines.program: The player now looks like a circle, but it only appears when the game creates it. Open {click}Program.
lines.drag-create: Drag {grab}create sprite player at x 160, y 120 under when the game starts. {snap}It fits right in.
lines.xy: The game screen is {w}320 pixels wide and {h}240 tall. {so}So x {x}160, y {y}120 is right in the middle.
lines.result: And there it is: {circle}your teal circle, in the middle of the screen.

code.text: Over here is the code. {code}This is the real DIV code your blocks made: {process}the player, with its circle, {create}and the line that creates it at {at}160, 120.
code.say: Over here is the code. This is the real [DIV](/dˈɪv/) code your blocks made: the player, with its circle, and the line that creates it at 160, 120.

lines.outro: Well done! {next}In lesson two, you'll make your circle move with the arrow keys.
